기계 점검 중에는 전원을 차단하고 조작 금지 표지판을 부착해야 합니다.During machine inspection, cut the power and affix an operation prohibition sign.
위험한 상황이 발생했을 때는 작업중지권을 발동하고 안전한 곳으로 대피하세요.When a dangerous situation occurs, invoke stop-work authority and evacuate safely.
기계에 손이 끼이는 협착 사고를 방지하기 위해 방호장치를 절대 해제하지 마세요.Never disable safety guards in order to prevent mechanical pinch-point accidents.
업무 중 부상을 당한 경우 외국인 근로자도 산재보험 혜택을 전액 받을 수 있습니다.Foreign workers who suffer on-the-job injuries are fully covered by accident insurance.

For industrial injury compensation claims, contact the Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service at 1588-0075.

item.title: Reading a Korean Mobile Phone Contract: Plans, Commitments, and Penalties
item.description: Understand your Korean mobile phone contract (통신 가입신청서). Learn how contract periods (약정기간), terminal installment fees, early cancellation penalties, and MVNOs work.
item.content:encoded:
In South Korea, a mobile phone number is vastly more than a communication tool—it serves as your universal digital national identity. Every online banking transfer, grocery delivery order, parcel tracking request, and government immigration portal relies on telecom-based identity verification (휴대폰 본인인증). Because this verification system requires an active phone line registered to your exact legal name, signing a mobile subscription agreement (이동통신 가입신청서) is an essential milestone.

However, commercial retail shops often present complex multi-page service agreements packed with jargon regarding installment financing, optional add-on services, and contractual lock-in periods. Understanding the fine print ensures you select the most economical plan while steering clear of surprise cancellation penalties. Below is an annotated breakdown of a standard Korean mobile phone contract.

The power of phone identity verification (본인확인)

In South Korea, your mobile phone is an official electronic signature. Through the nationwide PASS application or simple SMS verification codes (문자 본인확인), service providers verify that you are the genuine account holder. To ensure this works seamlessly, your telecom subscription must be registered under your physical Alien Registration Card (ARC), not a temporary tourist passport.

If you initially purchased a 90-day prepaid SIM using your passport upon arrival, visit an official carrier retail branch the moment your physical ARC is issued. Request an Alien Registration Information Update (외국인등록번호 명의변경/실명전환). This simple administrative step connects your existing phone number directly to your registered legal alien identity.

Big Three carriers versus Budget Phone MVNOs (알뜰폰)

The Korean telecommunications landscape is dominated by the 'Big Three' Mobile Network Operators (MNOs): SK Telecom (SKT), KT, and LG Uplus (LGU+). While they operate physical customer centers and offer extensive membership perks (멤버십 할인), their monthly plans generally range between 50,000 KRW and 90,000 KRW with two-year mandatory contracts.

For budget-conscious international residents, Mobile Virtual Network Operators (MVNOs), widely called 알뜰폰 (Affordable Phones), offer significant savings. MVNOs rent transmission towers directly from the Big Three, guaranteeing identical 4G LTE and 5G call quality and network speeds for half the price—often between 15,000 KRW and 30,000 KRW per month. Best of all, most MVNO plans are SIM-only (USIM 요금제) with zero contractual lock-in periods.

Handset subsidies versus 25% monthly plan discounts

When buying a new smartphone through a major carrier, Korean law gives you an either-or choice regarding discounts. Option A is the Device Subsidy (공시지원금), which provides an upfront cash discount off the retail purchase price of the phone. Option B is the Selective Contract Discount (선택약정할인), which deducts exactly 25 percent off your monthly plan fee every billing cycle for 12 or 24 months.

In almost all cases, selecting the 25 percent monthly discount yields much larger cumulative savings over two years, especially if you enroll in high-data or unlimited plans. Furthermore, if you bring an unlocked smartphone purchased overseas or bought outright from manufacturers (자급제폰), you can immediately sign up for the 25 percent selective discount without buying any new equipment.

Verifying device eligibility via IMEI lookups

Before bringing a second-hand smartphone or overseas device into a Korean telecom shop, check its 15-digit International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number. Dialing *#06# on your device keypad displays the IMEI instantly. You can enter this sequence into the official Korean Association for ICT Promotion portal (imei.kr) to verify two critical safety points.

First, the system verifies that the handset is not flagged as lost or stolen (분실·도난 여부 확인). Second, it verifies whether the handset is eligible for the 25 percent monthly plan discount (25% 요금할인 대상 단말기 조회). If a previous owner enrolled the device in an unfinished 24-month contract, the system will block selective discounts until the original obligation is formally resolved.

Early cancellation penalties and departing Korea

Before signing a 24-month contract, evaluate how long you plan to remain in South Korea. If your work visa or study program concludes in 12 months, signing a two-year contract is risky. Terminating the contract prematurely triggers an Early Termination Penalty (위약금 or 할인반환금).

Under Korean telecom formulas, the carrier claws back the monthly 25 percent discounts you enjoyed during the earlier months of the contract. Additionally, any remaining installments on your handset hardware balance must be paid in full upon cancellation. If your visa duration is under two years, opt for a 12-month selective contract or choose an uncontracted MVNO SIM plan.

🧀자급제 휴대폰을 가지고 있는데 요금 할인을 받을 수 있나요?
🥔네, 선택약정할인을 신청하시면 매달 요금의 25%를 할인받으실 수 있습니다.
🧀1년 약정과 2년 약정 중에서 선택할 수 있나요?
🥔네, 체류 기간에 맞춰 1년 약정을 선택하셔도 동일하게 25% 할인이 적용됩니다.

Essential telecom vocabulary

외국인등록증 발급 후 통신사에 방문하여 여권 명의를 등록증 명의로 전환했습니다.After receiving my ARC, I visited the telecom branch to switch my passport identity to my ARC.
알뜰폰 요금제는 약정 기간 없이 저렴한 기본료로 통신 서비스를 이용할 수 있습니다.MVNO budget plans let you use telecom services at low rates with no commitment period.
선택약정할인을 통해 매달 이동통신 기본요금의 25%를 감면받고 있습니다.Through the selective discount, I receive a 25% monthly reduction off my base telecom bill.
약정 기간 만료 전에 해지할 경우 누적된 할인반환금이 청구될 수 있습니다.If you terminate before contract expiration, accumulated discount penalties may be billed.
휴대폰 본인인증을 통과해야 한국의 주요 온라인 서비스에 가입할 수 있습니다.You must pass mobile identity verification to sign up for major Korean online services.
자급제 단말기를 구입하면 통신사 약정이나 부가서비스 가입 의무가 없습니다.Buying an unlocked phone frees you from telecom contract terms or required add-ons.
Conditions and SuppositionsA/V-아/어도Means that even in such a situation, the outcome remains unchanged.Use this concessive grammar pattern when discussing plan terms, contract durations, and scenarios where penalties apply regardless of circumstances.Write your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for
Telecom dispute mediation and IMEI verificationTo verify if an unlocked phone qualifies for the 25% selective discount, check its IMEI at the Korea Association for ICT Promotion portal (imei.kr). For unfair retail sales practices, unauthorized contracts, or penalty disputes, contact the Korea Communications Commission helpline at 1335.

item.title: Reading Korean Delivery Messages: Tracking, Drop-Off Requests, and Locker Codes
item.description: Master Korean parcel delivery notifications (택배 문자). Learn how to track shipments, specify drop-off locations, retrieve packages from smart lockers, and contact couriers.
item.content:encoded:
South Korea is globally renowned for its hyper-efficient logistics networks, where online orders placed late at night arrive at your doorstep before sunrise. Whether you order fresh groceries via dawn delivery (새벽배송) or household goods through regular parcel services, communication between couriers and customers is maintained through automated text messages and KakaoTalk notifications (알림톡).

For foreign residents who cannot read Korean rapidly, deciphering shipping alerts, building entrance access codes, and locker combination pins can mean the difference between a smooth delivery and a missing parcel. Below is an annotated breakdown of a standard Korean parcel delivery notification.

The language of Korean parcel tracking

When you buy items through Korean e-commerce platforms like Coupang, Naver Shopping, or Gmarket, you will receive real-time status updates at each logistics milestone. The progression begins with 상품준비중 (preparing shipment), moves to 집화완료 (picked up by courier), enters the regional consolidation hub (간선상하차), and finally switches to 배송출발 (out for delivery).

On the morning of the delivery date, an automated message arrives stating your estimated delivery timeframe (배송 예정 시간). At this juncture, the message usually contains an interactive link allowing you to update delivery preferences or provide temporary entrance codes if you will not be home.

Selecting drop-off spots: Front door versus security desks

In South Korea, unattended doorstep delivery (문 앞 배송) is standard practice due to exceptionally low petty theft rates and widespread CCTV surveillance in residential hallways. However, if your building lacks an elevator, does not have security cameras, or opens directly onto an exposed public street, you may prefer safer alternatives.

You can instruct the courier to deposit parcels at the 경비실 (building security office), where guards log boxes into a ledger. In single-family residential alleys or low-rise villas without guards, some residents request items to be tucked inside the outdoor fire hydrant box (소화전 함) or behind the exterior shoe cabinet (신발장 안) to keep them out of public view.

Navigating smart parcel lockers (무인택배함)

Many modern residential complexes, officetels, and municipal subway stations feature automated electronic parcel lockers known as 무인택배함. If a courier drops your package in a smart locker, you will receive an SMS containing two vital pieces of information: the locker cabinet number (보관함 번호) and a temporary four- to six-digit passcode (비밀번호).

To retrieve your parcel, approach the central touch kiosk, tap 물품 찾기 (Retrieve Item), type in your apartment unit number, enter the designated locker number, and key in the secret passcode. Some commercial lockers enforce a free storage window of 24 to 48 hours; exceeding this period incurs small daily storage penalties.

Convenience store pickup networks and managing returns

If you live alone or frequently travel for work, receiving home deliveries can feel inconvenient. South Korea's omnipresent 24-hour convenience store chains—notably GS25 and CU—offer dedicated branch pickup services known as 반값택배 (Half-Price Delivery) or 알뜰택배. When ordering online, you can designate a neighborhood store branch as the delivery destination; the store clerks hold your box behind the counter until you present the barcode on your smartphone.

Furthermore, returning unwanted purchases (반품) is remarkably straightforward. Most e-commerce mobile applications allow you to request automated return pickup (반품 회수 요청). You simply re-tape the original parcel box, write your order number on the exterior carton, and leave it outside your apartment front door before 09:00 AM on the scheduled pickup morning. The courier collects the package and leaves an automated pickup receipt via text.

Etiquette for contacting couriers and resolving lost parcels

Korean couriers handle grueling delivery quotas. If you must adjust delivery instructions or ask about a delayed box, avoid calling repeatedly while they are driving or carrying heavy packages up staircases. Instead, send a brief, courteous text message including your address and unit number.

If a notification announces 배송 완료 (delivery completed) but your parcel is nowhere to be found, check the photo proof link first. It may turn out the box was placed in front of your neighbor's door or left with security. If the item was genuinely misdelivered or lost, notify the shopping platform customer service center (고객센터) immediately to initiate an insurance reimbursement or complimentary replacement.

🧀기사님, 오늘 배송 예정인 택배를 문 앞에 두고 가 주시겠어요?
🥔네, 알겠습니다. 공동현관 비밀번호를 문자로 남겨 주시면 올라가겠습니다.

🥔확인했습니다. 문 앞에 배송 후 완료 사진을 전송해 드리겠습니다.

Essential delivery vocabulary

운송장번호를 택배사 웹사이트에 입력하여 실시간 배송 위치를 조회했습니다.I entered the tracking number on the courier website to view the real-time location.

공동현관 비밀번호를 정확하게 기재해야 기사님이 세대 앞까지 올라올 수 있습니다.You must record the entrance code correctly so the courier can reach your door.
무인택배함 보관 문자에 적힌 인증번호를 입력하고 물건을 찾았습니다.I entered the passcode from the smart locker text message and retrieved the parcel.
배송 완료 알림톡에 첨부된 사진을 통해 물품 도착 여부를 확인했습니다.I verified the item arrival through the photo attached to the completion notice.

For unresolved consumer compensation disputes, dial 1372 (Korea Consumer Agency).

item.title: Reading a Korean Apartment Maintenance Bill: General Fees, Heating, and Electricity
item.description: Demystify your monthly Korean apartment maintenance statement (관리비 고지서). Learn how common fees, electricity, water, city gas heating, and payment deadlines work.
item.content:encoded:
Every month, residential tenants in South Korea receive an itemized building maintenance statement, commonly termed a 관리비 고지서 (maintenance bill). Whether slipped under your front door or deposited into your lobby mailbox, this document details building management costs alongside your personal electricity, water, and heating consumption.

For newcomers unfamiliar with Korean communal housing systems, deciphering the difference between shared common fees and private utility usage can prevent costly surprises. Below is an annotated breakdown of a standard Korean apartment and officetel maintenance invoice.

Shared building overhead versus individual household consumption

Korean maintenance invoices are divided into two distinct sections: shared communal costs (공용 관리비) and individual consumption charges (개별 사용료). Common maintenance fees are apportioned across all residents based on their apartment unit's registered floor area (전용면적). These include general management, elevator electricity, hallway lighting, communal disinfection, and fire safety inspections.

Individual consumption charges reflect your personal lifestyle. Hallway meter readers inspect your private dials every month to record kilowatt-hours of power, cubic meters of water, and gigacalories of district heating. Being conscious of your daily consumption directly curbs this portion of the bill.

Electricity billing and the progressive tariff trap

Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) applies a progressive tariff structure (누진제) to residential electricity. Consumption is divided into three volume tiers. If your household remains in Tier 1 (under 200 kWh per month), electricity is inexpensive. However, pushing past Tier 2 (over 400 kWh) causes the per-kilowatt rate to jump dramatically.

During sweltering summer months, running older air conditioners on maximum blast 24 hours a day can catapult your household into Tier 3, resulting in bills that double or triple unexpectedly. Using energy-saving inverter units and setting thermostats between 25 and 26 degrees Celsius keeps consumption within affordable brackets.

Heating systems: District heating versus individual city gas

South Korean homes use ondol (온돌), a traditional radiant underfloor heating system. The mechanism powering your floor depends on the building type. Modern large apartment complexes frequently use District Heating (지역난방), where hot water piped from regional plants warms floors and provides domestic tap water; this fee appears directly on your main apartment maintenance bill.

In villas, officetels, and studio flats (원룸), homes usually feature individual gas boilers (개별난방). In these properties, your maintenance bill covers only common upkeep and water, while heating and cooking fuel arrive via a separate monthly City Gas (도시가스) envelope. In winter, never turn the boiler off completely when leaving for work; switch it to Out-of-Home Mode (외출 모드) to prevent pipes from freezing (동파) while avoiding the surge in fuel needed to reheat freezing water.

Settling bills: Virtual accounts, auto-debit, and payment deadlines

At the bottom of your bill, the management office prints dedicated Virtual Bank Accounts (가상계좌) under major banks like Shinhan, Woori, and KB. You can pay via mobile banking transfer, register for monthly automatic bank withdrawal (자동이체), or pay at convenience store registers by scanning the printed barcode before the deadline (납부기한).

Missing the deadline incurs a 2 percent late surcharge (연체료). Furthermore, prolonged utility arrears can lead to service suspensions. If you plan to travel abroad for several weeks, ensure your auto-debit account has sufficient funds to avoid unpaid balances.

Moving out: Claiming your Long-Term Repair Reserve refund

Here is a crucial money-saving tip every renter in Korea must know: inspect your bill for an item called 장기수선충당금 (Long-Term Repair Reserve Fund). Under the Housing Act, this fund finances major building structural restorations like exterior painting and elevator replacements. By law, this is the legal property owner's obligation, not the tenant's.

Because the management office bills it alongside monthly maintenance for convenience, tenants pay it upfront. When your lease terminates and you move out, request a payment certificate (장기수선충당금 납부확인서) from the management office. Hand this document to your landlord, and they are legally required to reimburse the cumulative sum—often amounting to several hundred thousand won—directly to you in cash or bank transfer.

item.title: Opening a Korean Bank Account: Application Forms, ARC Rules, and Limit Accounts
item.description: Step-by-step walkthrough of opening a bank account in South Korea. Learn how to complete the application form, overcome limit account (한도제한계좌) caps, and set up mobile banking.
item.content:encoded:
Establishing a domestic commercial bank account is one of the very first financial milestones for any international resident arriving in South Korea. Without an active local bank account, receiving monthly wages, transferring apartment deposits, setting up recurring utility auto-debits, and purchasing public transit passes becomes nearly impossible.

However, South Korea enforces stringent anti-fraud regulations and the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act (금융실명제). To open an account without multiple frustrating trips to the teller window, you must understand the mandatory customer questionnaire, identity verification rules, and documentation needed to lift restrictive daily transfer caps. Below is an annotated breakdown of a standard Korean bank account application form.

The Real-Name Financial System and the 100% name match rule

Under Korea's Real-Name Financial Transactions Act, financial institutions are legally barred from opening accounts under nicknames, shortened initials, or unverified aliases. For foreign nationals, your legal name in banking databases must match your physical Alien Registration Card down to the single space. If your passport displays middle names, ensure the teller enters them in the identical sequence.

A tiny spelling discrepancy will prevent you from completing telecom identity authentication (본인확인). Because Korean online shopping portals, food delivery apps, and mobile payments authenticate identity by comparing your telecom subscriber name with bank records, maintaining perfect name synchronization across your alien registration, SIM card, and bank account is critical.

Conquering the 'Limit Account' (한도제한계좌) obstacle

To curb voice phishing syndicates and illegal account trafficking, Korean regulators require banks to classify all newly opened checking accounts as Transaction Limit Accounts (한도제한계좌) unless definitive proof of financial purpose is furnished. In a limit account, your daily electronic transfers via smartphone banking and ATM withdrawals are capped between 300,000 KRW and 1,000,000 KRW.

While 300,000 KRW suffices for grocery shopping, it makes paying monthly rent or wiring money to family back home virtually impossible. To unlock normal account limits on day one, bring proof of purpose (금융거래 목적 확인서류). For employed workers, present your signed standard employment contract (근로계약서), a recent certificate of employment (재직증명서), or company business registration certificate (사업자등록증 사본).

Alternative methods to lift transaction limits later

If you are an international student, job seeker (D-10), or working holiday visa holder without an immediate employment certificate, your initial account will be opened as a limit account. Do not panic; you can upgrade the account after establishing a regular transaction pattern.

Most commercial banks will lift transfer restrictions if you maintain three consecutive months of automatic salary transfers (급여이체), set up recurring automated utility debits (공과금 자동이체) for phone or electricity bills, or demonstrate consistent card spending on your linked debit card. Once these criteria are met, visit the branch with your ARC and bankbook (통장) to remove the ceiling.

Designating your foreign exchange bank for overseas remittances

Sending money back home to support family or repay student loans requires compliance with South Korea's Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (외국환거래법). Under these laws, every resident foreign national must select and designate a single commercial bank branch as their Designated Foreign Exchange Bank (거래외국환은행 지정).

When opening your account, ask the bank clerk to complete this designation on the spot. You will need to show your passport, ARC, and employment contract proving earned income in Korea. Once registered, you gain access to streamlined digital remittance channels with significantly discounted exchange rates, lower wire transfer fees, and the ability to send funds 24/7 directly from your banking smartphone application without making monthly branch visits.

Check cards, transit chips, and digital certificates

When completing the application, always request a Check Card (체크카드)—the Korean equivalent of a Visa or Mastercard debit card. Ask the teller specifically for a card with built-in postpaid transit capabilities (후불교통카드). This allows you to tap subway turnstiles and city buses nationwide without preloading separate plastic T-money cards; charges are automatically settled from your account once a month.

Finally, have the banker assist you in installing the bank's mobile application and generating a Financial Certificate (금융인증서) or Joint Certificate (공동인증서). Securely store your account password (4 digits) and digital transfer PIN (6 digits). Never share your physical security card (보안카드) or OTP device numbers with anyone claiming to represent police or tax officers.

🧀서류를 제출하면 일일 이체 한도 제한을 바로 해제할 수 있나요?
🥔네, 재직 서류로 급여 목적이 확인되면 일반 계좌로 개설하여 한도를 풀어 드립니다.

Essential banking vocabulary

한도제한계좌는 모바일 뱅킹을 통한 하루 이체 금액이 제한됩니다.A transaction limit account restricts the daily transfer amount via mobile banking.
급여 이체 실적이 3개월 이상 쌓이면 한도 해제를 신청할 수 있습니다.Once salary deposits accumulate for three months, you can apply to lift limits.
후불교통 기능이 포함된 체크카드로 버스와 지하철을 편리하게 이용합니다.I conveniently use buses and subways with a check card featuring postpaid transit.
전자금융 거래 시 필요한 보안카드와 비밀번호를 안전하게 보관해야 합니다.You must securely store the security card and passwords needed for digital transactions.

item.title: Filling Out a Korean Hospital Intake Form: Symptoms, History, and Prescriptions
item.description: Navigate medical visits in South Korea with confidence. Learn how to fill out clinic intake forms (문진표), describe symptom progression, report allergies, and pick up pharmacy prescriptions.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking medical care in a foreign country can be intimidating, especially when illness strikes suddenly and medical terminology feels unfamiliar. Fortunately, South Korea boasts one of the most accessible and efficient healthcare systems in the world. Walk-in consultations at neighborhood primary care clinics (의원) require no weeks-long waitlists, and consultations are remarkably affordable under National Health Insurance.

Upon arriving at an internal medicine clinic (내과), orthopedic center (정형외과), or ENT specialist (이비인후과), the reception desk will hand you a first-visit questionnaire known as a 문진표 (medical intake questionnaire). Filling out this document accurately ensures that attending physicians diagnose your condition swiftly without prescribing contraindicated drugs. Below is an annotated breakdown of a standard Korean clinic intake form.

At reception: Insurance verification and clinic tiers

In South Korea, medical institutions are organized into three tiers: primary neighborhood clinics (1차 의원), general secondary hospitals (2차 병원), and tertiary university medical centers (3차 상급종합병원). For colds, mild sprains, skin rashes, or digestive issues, visit a local neighborhood clinic first. You do not need a prior appointment; simply walk in during clinic operating hours and present your Alien Registration Card (외국인등록증) or mobile health insurance pass.

The receptionist checks your national health database record within seconds. Under statutory National Health Insurance (국민건강보험), patients typically pay only 20 to 30 percent of primary consultation costs out of pocket, with basic visits often costing less than 10,000 KRW including diagnostic tests. If you require specialized tertiary hospital care, you must first obtain a referral slip (진료의뢰서) from a primary clinic to qualify for insurance coverage.

Describing pain and symptoms with precise Korean terms

Korean medical vocabulary offers rich, descriptive nuances for physical discomfort. When speaking to the physician or filling out the intake form, choosing the right adjective makes an immediate difference. For headaches or muscle aches, 욱신거리다 describes a throbbing, pulsating sensation, while 지끈거리다 captures a splitting tension headache. If pain feels like sharp needles pricking your skin or nerves, use 콕콕 쑤시다 or 찌릿하다.

For gastrointestinal distress, 속이 메스껍다 signifies nausea, whereas 속이 쓰리다 indicates burning acid reflux or stomach irritation. If your joints or back feel heavy and stiff, doctors recognize 뻐근하다 or 묵직하다. When tracking fever, tell the doctor whether chills accompanied the temperature (오한이 들다) and whether the fever responded to over-the-counter antipyretics.

Drug safety and the national DUR checking network

When the doctor inputs your prescription into their clinical software, Korea's nationwide Drug Utilization Review (DUR) system automatically audits the selected compounds against your prescription history across all clinics in real time. The DUR system flags dangerous duplicate ingredients or harmful pharmacological interactions before the doctor prints the order.

However, the electronic DUR network cannot track over-the-counter remedies, imported medications, or undocumented drug allergies. That is why completing Section 6 on your intake form is vital. If you ever experienced hives (두드러기), facial swelling (부종), or shortness of breath (호흡 곤란) after taking antibiotics or pain relievers, make sure the physician records the allergy on your permanent clinic profile.

Receiving your prescription and visiting the pharmacy

At the conclusion of your consultation, the clinic desk issues two copies of your medical prescription (처방전)—one marked for the dispensing pharmacy (약국 제출용) and one for your personal records (환자 보관용). Take the pharmacy copy to any dispensary located right outside the clinic or nearby.

Korean pharmacies pack your tablets into transparent individualized dose packets (약포지) labeled with morning, afternoon, or evening icons. The paper medicine bag (약봉투) doubles as an official legal receipt and drug manual, detailing the active chemical names of each pill, photographic identification guides, and dietary recommendations such as taking doses 30 minutes after meals (식후 30분).

Claiming private insurance: Documents to request

If you hold private Korean indemnity medical insurance (실손의료보험) or overseas travel health coverage, you can recover a major portion of your out-of-pocket clinic and pharmacy costs. Before leaving the clinic, ask the front desk for an itemized medical expense receipt (진료비 영수증) and a detailed calculation statement (진료비 세부내역서). Both documents are issued free of charge upon request.

For small claims under 100,000 KRW, most domestic insurance mobile apps allow you to snap photos of your pharmacy medicine bag and clinic receipt to receive reimbursements within 24 to 48 hours without submitting physical doctor certificates.

🧀어제 저녁부터 열이 나고 목이 심하게 부어서 진료를 받고 싶습니다.
🥔네, 외국인등록증을 보여주시고 이 문진표의 증상과 복용 중인 약을 적어 주세요.
🧀페니실린 계열 항생제에 두드러기 반응이 있는데 여기에 표시하면 되나요?
🥔네, 알레르기 항목에 적어 주시면 원장님께서 다른 계열 약으로 처방해 주십니다.

Essential clinic and symptom vocabulary

외국인등록번호로 건강보험 가입 여부를 접수처에서 바로 조회할 수 있습니다.At reception, your health insurance coverage can be verified immediately using your ARC number.
약물 알레르기가 있는 경우 문진표에 반드시 적어 의사에게 알려야 합니다.If you have drug allergies, you must write them on the intake form to inform the doctor.
감기 증상이 심해져서 동네 내과 의원에 진료를 받으러 갔습니다.As my cold symptoms became worse, I went to a local internal medicine clinic for treatment.
진료가 끝난 후 처방전 2부 중 1부를 인근 약국에 제출했습니다.After consultation, I submitted one of the two prescription copies to a nearby pharmacy.
약봉투 겉면에 적힌 복용법과 주의사항을 꼼꼼하게 읽어 보았습니다.I carefully read the dosage instructions and precautions printed on the medicine packet.
상급종합병원에서 진료를 받으려면 1차 의료기관의 진료의뢰서가 필요합니다.To receive care at a tertiary general hospital, a referral slip from a primary clinic is required.

For after-hours non-emergency medical inquiries, night-duty pharmacies, or hospital navigation in English, call the 1330 Korea Travel Hotline (interpretation available) or the Dasan Call Center at 120 in Seoul.

item.title: Reading a Korean Lease Contract: Security Deposits, Maintenance Fees, and Tenant Rights
item.description: Navigating a Korean residential lease agreement (부동산 임대차계약서). Learn how security deposits, monthly rent, management fees, special clauses, and fixed dates protect foreign tenants.
item.content:encoded:
Finding and renting an apartment, officetel, or studio flat (원룸) in South Korea is an exciting milestone for foreign workers, international students, and resident expatriates. However, Korea's unique rental structure—characterized by substantial security deposits (보증금) and intricate legal covenants—makes signing a lease contract (부동산 임대차계약서) a process where thorough legal diligence is paramount.

Whether you are renting through a monthly rent model (월세) or a lump-sum deposit lease (전세), understanding every paragraph in the standard real estate agreement shields your hard-earned money against landlord defaults and unexpected utility charges. Below is an annotated breakdown of a standard Korean residential lease contract.

Verifying the Certified Register: Debt ratios and ownership

Before putting any down payment on the table, demand a fresh copy of the Certified Real Estate Register (등기부등본), issued on the exact date of signing. In Section Eul (을구), inspect any collateral mortgages (근저당권) established by commercial banks or private lenders. The golden safety benchmark in Korean real estate states that the building's total debt plus the collective security deposits of all residents should never exceed 70 to 80 percent of the property's estimated market value.

Furthermore, cross-reference Section Gap (갑구) to confirm that the person sitting across the negotiation table is indeed the registered legal owner. Verify their National Identification Card or Alien Registration Card against the title deed. If an agent or family member signs on the owner's behalf, you must insist on a formal power of attorney (위임장) accompanied by the owner's official seal certificate (인감증명서).

The golden trio: Move-in, address change, and fixed date

Signing the lease is only half the battle; establishing legal priority over your deposit requires three simultaneous actions upon taking possession. First is taking actual physical occupancy (주택의 인도). Second is reporting your change of residence (체류지 변경신고 for foreigners, equivalent to 전입신고) within 14 days of moving. Third is receiving the Fixed Date stamp (확정일자) at your local community service center (주민센터) or registry office.

Together, these three steps create two vital legal protections under the Housing Lease Protection Act: opposing power (대항력), which prevents a new landlord or creditor from evicting you, and the preferential repayment right (우선변제권), which guarantees that your deposit will be reimbursed ahead of junior creditors if the building is placed in public auction.

Deposit guarantee insurance: An extra shield for foreign tenants

For added peace of mind, especially when placing deposits above twenty or thirty million won, consider subscribing to Deposit Return Guarantee Insurance (전세보증금 반환보증보험). Public guarantee bodies such as the Korea Housing & Urban Guarantee Corporation (HUG) and Seoul Guarantee Insurance (SGI) indemnify your full deposit if the lessor fails to repay it upon lease completion. Foreign residents with valid alien registration can apply through designated commercial banks or online guarantee portals by submitting a certified lease copy and proof of residency.

Deconstructing maintenance fees and utility bills

In recent years, many rental listings advertise attractive monthly rents while quietly imposing inflated monthly management fees (관리비). Always ask the licensed real estate broker (공인중개사) for an itemized breakdown of building maintenance. Standard building fees typically cover elevator upkeep, stairwell cleaning, security personnel, and common area lighting.

Some buildings bundle high-speed fiber internet and municipal water into the fixed maintenance fee, while city gas heating (도시가스) and household electricity are measured by individual household meters. Clarifying these terms prevents surprise bills during freezing Korean winter months when floor radiant heating (보일러) runs around the clock.

Special clauses and contract termination etiquette

Article 7 (특약사항) overrides generic assumptions and often contains decisive conditions regarding deposit deductions. Photograph every scratch, tile crack, or water stain on your first afternoon inside the apartment and send timestamped pictures to the landlord or broker. Korean courts distinguish between normal wear and tear (자연 마모) from ordinary living, which landlords must absorb, and intentional damage (훼손), which tenants must repair.

When your lease reaches its conclusion, notice must be served between two and six months before the expiration date if you intend to move out. If neither party communicates intentions during this window, the lease enters an implicit renewal (묵시적 갱신) under the same terms for another two years. Tenants who encounter implicit renewal can terminate the agreement anytime with three months' advance notice.

🥔네, 잔금을 치르고 입주하신 날에 바로 주민센터에서 체류지 변경 신고와 확정일자를 받으셔야 합니다.

🥔맞습니다. 서류를 제출하시면 계약서에 확정일자 도장을 바로 찍어 줍니다.

Essential lease vocabulary

이사한 날로부터 14일 이내에 관할 주민센터에 체류지 변경 신고를 마쳐야 합니다.You must complete the change of residence notification within 14 days of moving.
확정일자를 받아 두어야 경매 시 보증금을 우선하여 변제받을 수 있습니다.You must obtain a fixed date stamp to secure preferential repayment of your deposit in an auction.
특약사항에 명시되지 않은 수리 비용은 임대인과 사전에 협의해야 합니다.Repair costs not specified in special conditions must be discussed with the landlord in advance.
월세 외에 관리비에 어떤 항목이 포함되어 있는지 꼼꼼하게 따져 보세요.Carefully examine which specific items are included in the maintenance fee besides monthly rent.
임대차 계약이 묵시적으로 갱신되면 이전 계약과 동일한 조건으로 연장됩니다.If a lease is implicitly renewed, it extends under the exact same terms as the prior contract.

item.description: Demystify your monthly Korean wage statement (급여명세서). Learn how base pay, overtime premiums, the four social insurances, and income tax withholdings are calculated.
item.content:encoded:
Receiving your monthly pay slip in South Korea can feel overwhelming when confronted with a dense matrix of Korean payroll abbreviations, insurance subtractions, and tax withholdings. Yet understanding every line item on this document is essential for verifying that your employer has paid you accurately according to statutory labor regulations.

Under Article 48, Paragraph 2 of the Labor Standards Act (근로기준법), all employers throughout South Korea must provide an itemized wage statement (급여명세서) every payday, whether via printed paper, email, or mobile messaging. Failure to provide an itemized statement carries administrative fines up to 5,000,000 KRW. Use the annotated breakdown below to audit your own monthly pay.

Gross earnings: Calculating base wage and overtime premiums

Your total compensation begins with gross earnings (지급총액), which combines contractual base pay with performance or statutory allowances. For full-time employees working 40 hours per week, your base salary covers 209 standard hours per month, incorporating the mandatory weekly paid holiday (주휴수당). Dividing your base pay by 209 gives your ordinary hourly wage (통상시급).

This ordinary hourly wage is the mathematical basis for all statutory overtime allowances. When you work beyond 8 hours a day, the law guarantees time-and-a-half (150 percent). If overtime takes place late at night between 22:00 and 06:00, or during a public holiday, premiums stack together. For instance, working 4 overtime hours at night entitles you to base overtime (150%) plus night differential (50%), totaling 200 percent of your base hourly rate.

The statutory minimum wage sanity check

Every year, the Korean government announces a nationwide statutory minimum hourly wage (최저시급). To confirm that your monthly base salary is legally compliant, calculate your base wage divided by 209 contractual hours. If that resulting hourly number falls even one won below the prevailing minimum wage rate, your contract violates the Minimum Wage Act (최저임금법). Fixed overtime allowances or discretionary bonuses cannot be bundled together to mask a sub-minimum base salary.

The four social insurances: Who pays what?

South Korea's comprehensive social safety net (4대 사회보험) is funded through shared contributions between employees and employers. On your pay slip, deductions appear under the deduction total (공제총액). National Pension (국민연금) charges 9 percent of gross income, with 4.5 percent deducted from your wage and the remaining 4.5 percent paid directly by the employer. Foreign nationals on E-9, E-7, or F visas should review bilateral social security treaties, as many nationalities can claim a lump-sum refund (반환일시금) with accrued interest upon permanently departing South Korea.

National Health Insurance (국민건강보험) operates similarly, split evenly at roughly 3.5 percent each for worker and firm (the rate is reset every year), plus a small surcharge for long-term elderly care. Employment Insurance (고용보험) finances unemployment benefits and vocational training; employees contribute 0.9 percent. Crucially, Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance (산재보험) never appears as a deduction on your pay slip because it is funded 100 percent by the employer. If an employer ever deducts accident insurance from your wage, that deduction is strictly illegal.

Income tax withholding versus year-end tax settlement

Every month, your company withholds estimated national income tax (소득세) and local income tax (지방소득세) using the National Tax Service simplified tax withholding table (근로소득 간이세액표). Because this monthly figure is only an estimate based on income brackets and reported family dependents, it is reconciled every February during the Year-End Tax Settlement (연말정산).

During tax settlement, you submit receipts for qualifying medical expenditures, debit and credit card spending, public transportation costs, education expenses, and monthly rent payments. If too much tax was deducted across the prior year, you will receive a handsome tax refund on your February or March pay slip. Conversely, if insufficient tax was withheld, a secondary tax settlement deduction will be applied.

Auditing discrepancies and bank transfer validation

Always compare your pay slip with your personal work attendance records and your bank account transaction statement. Check whether all approved overtime hours, weekend shifts, and meal subsidies were included in the gross calculation. Article 43 of the Labor Standards Act mandates that wages must be paid in full, in legal currency, directly to the worker's own bank account on a fixed date every month.

Employers are strictly forbidden from paying through third parties, retaining wages as forced savings, or applying arbitrary deductions labeled as administrative fees or accommodation costs without prior written consent. If you notice any discrepancy between your pay slip total and the money entering your bank account, immediately request clarification from the accounting department in writing.

🥔네, 기본급을 209시간으로 나눈 시급에 1.5를 곱하여 정확히 지급되었습니다.

Essential pay slip vocabulary

산재보험료는 사업주가 전액 부담하므로 급여에서 공제하지 않습니다.Industrial accident insurance is fully paid by the employer, so it is not deducted from wages.
연말정산을 통해 지난 1년간 납부한 세금을 정확하게 정산합니다.Through the year-end tax settlement, taxes paid over the past year are accurately adjusted.
실지급액은 지급총액에서 4대 보험과 세금을 공제한 나머지 금액입니다.The net pay is the remaining amount after deducting four major insurances and taxes from gross earnings.

Conditions and SuppositionsA/V-(으)면Means 'if' or 'when' something happens. Widely used for conditions and suppositions.Use this conditional pattern when explaining payroll requirements, overtime thresholds, and eligibility criteria for allowances.Write your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for

item.title: Reading a Korean Employment Contract: Key Clauses and Common Traps
item.description: Before signing a standard employment contract in Korea, examine these essential clauses. Learn how working hours, rest periods, overtime wages, dormitory deductions, and social insurance are documented.
item.content:encoded:
Every international resident working in South Korea must sign a written employment contract before beginning work. Under Article 17 of Korea's Labor Standards Act (근로기준법), employers are legally obligated to issue a signed duplicate copy detailing mandatory working conditions directly to the employee. Verbal promises made during interviews or informal hiring chats carry virtually no weight in wage disputes, labor arbitration hearings, or immigration audits.

For workers holding E-9 non-professional employment visas, E-7 specialized occupation visas, D-10 job seeker visas, F-visa family residents, or working holiday visas, the standard employment contract (표준근로계약서) serves as the legal bedrock for your lawful stay and labor rights. Before picking up a pen or stamping your personal seal (도장), review the document line by line against the annotated example below.

Contracted hours versus overtime: The 209-hour standard

In South Korea, standard full-time employment is legally defined as 40 hours per week (8 hours per day, 5 days per week). When calculating monthly salaries, the Ministry of Employment and Labor adds 8 weekly paid holiday hours to the 40 worked hours, totaling 48 paid hours per week. Multiplying 48 hours by the average 4.345 weeks in a month yields the famous 209-hour standard.

Any labor performed beyond your 8 daily contracted hours constitutes overtime work (연장근로). Overtime, night work performed between 22:00 and 06:00 (야간근로), and holiday shifts (휴일근로) must each be compensated with an extra 50 percent premium above your ordinary hourly wage (통상임금). Total combined overtime cannot exceed 12 hours per week under Korea's 52-hour statutory workweek cap. Keep your own calendar log of punch-in and punch-out stamps to compare against your monthly pay slip.

Weekly holiday allowance: Demystifying 주휴수당

Many foreign employees are surprised to find extra paid hours on their contract. Under Article 55 of the Labor Standards Act, any worker who logs at least 15 scheduled hours per week and completes all agreed shifts must receive at least one paid day off every week. This statutory entitlement is called 주휴수당 (weekly holiday allowance).

If an employer pays by the hour or day instead of a fixed monthly salary, verify whether the quoted hourly rate already bundles weekly holiday pay or excludes it. If your contract states an hourly wage without clear notation, your employer must calculate and add weekly holiday hours whenever you maintain full attendance during the working week. Clear documentation prevents wage shortfalls at the end of the month.

Annual paid leave entitlements (연차유급휴가)

Another crucial right frequently overlooked is statutory annual paid leave under Article 60 of the Labor Standards Act. During your first year of employment, you accrue one day of paid vacation for every month of perfect attendance, up to a maximum of 11 days. After completing your first full year with at least 80 percent attendance, you receive 15 days of paid annual leave. If you do not use these days due to business needs, unused leave must be compensated as cash allowance upon contract conclusion.

Probation periods and legal wage limits

Employers frequently request a probation period (수습기간). Korean labor law permits companies to pay 90 percent of the statutory minimum wage during probation, but only under strict legal criteria: the total contract duration must be one year or longer, and the reduced rate cannot apply for more than three months. For simple manual labor roles designated by national occupational standards, no wage deduction is permitted even during probation. If your contract is for ten or eleven months, any probation discount is completely unlawful.

Dormitory deductions and severance pay safeguards

A common point of dispute for overseas workers involves housing and utilities deductions. Under Ministry guidelines, employers cannot unilaterally withdraw money from your pay packet for food or dormitory accommodation. Any deduction requires a separate written consent form (기숙사비 공제 동의서) clearly stating the accommodation type, facilities provided, and itemized monthly fees. Temporary container units or makeshift structures have strict deduction caps and safety standards.

Furthermore, every worker who remains with an enterprise for one full year or longer is entitled to statutory severance pay (퇴직금), equivalent to at least 30 days of average wages for each consecutive year of service. For E-9 workers, employers are mandated to deposit monthly premiums into Departure Guarantee Insurance (출국만기보험). If the accumulated insurance fund upon departure falls short of your legal severance entitlement, the employer is legally obligated to settle the remaining balance in cash before you leave the country.

🥔맞습니다. 이번 계약은 1년 계약이므로 해당 법적 기준을 정확히 준수하고 있습니다.

Essential contract vocabulary

표준근로계약서 사본 1부를 근로자에게 반드시 교부해야 합니다.The employer must deliver one copy of the standard employment contract to the worker.
소정근로시간을 초과하여 일하면 연장근로수당이 지급됩니다.If you work beyond the contracted working hours, overtime allowance will be paid.
주 15시간 이상 일하고 개근하면 주휴수당을 받을 권리가 생깁니다.If you work 15 or more hours per week without unexcused absences, you earn weekly holiday pay.
수습기간 중이라도 4대 보험은 첫날부터 의무적으로 가입해야 합니다.Even during probation, the four major social insurances must be registered from day one.
기숙사비나 식대를 급여에서 공제하려면 사전에 서면 동의서가 필요합니다.To deduct dormitory or meal expenses from wages, prior written consent is required.

For visa transfer regulations, consult the Immigration Contact Center at 1345.

item.title: TOPIK writing Q54: how to structure the essay
item.description: Question 54 awards up to 50 points, yet many test takers lose marks despite flawless grammar because their essay structure is disorganized. Here is the standard outline that scorers expect.
item.content:encoded:
Question 54 of the TOPIK II exam asks you to write an argumentative essay of 600 to 700 characters. Worth 50 points, it frequently determines whether a test taker achieves Level 4 or Level 6. Scorers routinely penalise essays that have zero spelling mistakes simply because the underlying paragraph structure lacks logical coherence.

Because time pressure in the writing section is intense, memorising a predictable structural framework before exam day is the single most reliable way to score 40 points or higher.

Every prompt contains two or three sub-questions

Under the main topic description, the test sheet lists two or three bullet points. Treat these bullet points as your paragraph blueprint. Dedicating exactly one body paragraph to each bullet point guarantees you answer every required grading criterion.

If a prompt asks: 1. Why is lifelong learning necessary? 2. What difficulties do adults face when learning? 3. What measures are needed to support them? — your essay must follow this exact sequence across paragraphs 2, 3, and 4.

Introduction: Do not copy the prompt

The single most common deduction in the introduction is copying sentences directly from the question sheet. Scorers disregard copied lines when calculating total character count. Open your essay by framing why the issue matters in your own words in two or three sentences.

Common mistakeParaphrasing only one particle from the prompt still counts as plagiarising the question prompt. Always introduce the topic using fresh vocabulary.

A reliable formula for your opening sentence is stating a broad social phenomenon: 「최근 우리 사회에서는 ~에 대한 관심이 높아지고 있다」 (Recently in our society, interest in ~ has been rising) or 「현대 사회에서 ~은 중요한 문제로 부각되고 있다」 (In modern society, ~ is emerging as a critical issue).

Body paragraphs: One claim plus evidence

Never list bare opinions without justification. Structure each body paragraph with a clear opening claim followed by concrete reasoning or real-world examples.

현대 사회에서 평생 교육은 필수적이다. 기술이 빠르게 변화하여 새로운 지식을 습득해야 하기 때문이다.Lifelong education is essential in modern society, because rapid technological change requires acquiring new knowledge.
Purpose and IntentionN을/를 위해서, V-기 위해서Says what the purpose is. It suits writing.State public goals and personal purposes in formal essay argumentsWrite your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for

Connect your ideas using written transition words like 「이에 따라」 (accordingly), 「반면에」 (on the other hand), and 「따라서」 (therefore), rather than conversational fillers like 그리고 or 그래서.

Changes in Parts of Speech관형형 -(으)ㄴ/-는/-(으)ㄹ NChanges verbs and adjectives into forms that attach in front of nouns to modify them.Use relative clauses to construct sophisticated formal noun phrasesWrite your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for

Conclusion: Synthesise without introducing new arguments

Your conclusion should briefly summarise your core arguments and offer a forward-looking recommendation or social call to action. Never introduce an entirely new argument in the final sentence.

Close with formal necessity structures such as 「-(으)ㄹ 필요가 있다」 (there is a need to), 「-(으)려고 노력해야 한다」 (efforts must be made to), or 「-는 것이 바람직하다」 (it is desirable that).

Use the plain written style (-는다 / -다)

Never write Question 54 in conversational polite styles (해요체 or 합니다체). Academic essays must be written in the plain narrative style (해라체), ending in 「-는다/다」, 「-(으)ㄹ 필요가 있다」, or 「-는 것이 바람직하다」.

  • Action verbs: -(느)ㄴ다 (생각한다, 발생한다, 증가한다)
  • Descriptive adjectives: -다 without ㄴ/는 (중요하다, 심각하다, 필요하다)
  • Copula nouns: -이다 / -가 아니다 (문제이다, 원인이 아니다)
  • Past tense: -았다/었다 (나타났다, 발전했다)
  • Future and conjecture: -(으)ㄹ 것이다 / -(으)ㄹ 것으로 보인다

Mastering the manuscript grid (원고지) layout

Writing on manuscript paper follows precise spacing rules that examiners inspect during grading. Violating basic grid formatting costs valuable points even when your text is well written.

  • Indent the very first square of every new paragraph by exactly one blank space
  • Never leave a blank square at the start of normal continuing lines inside a paragraph
  • Place periods, commas, and quotation marks in the bottom-left corner of their own square
  • Write Arabic numbers and Latin letters two per square (e.g. '20' or 'AI' share a single box)
  • If punctuation falls at the end of a line, write it in the margin rather than starting a new line with a period

Time allocation strategy for the 50-minute writing section

The TOPIK II writing test allows exactly 50 minutes for Questions 51 through 54. Running out of time on Question 54 is the number one cause of failed score goals.

  1. Minutes 0 to 10: Complete Question 51 and Question 52 (fill-in-the-blank short questions)
  2. Minutes 10 to 25: Complete Question 53 (data and graph description, 200 to 300 characters)
  3. Minutes 25 to 30: Outline Question 54 (brainstorm keywords and assign bullet points to paragraphs)
  4. Minutes 30 to 48: Write Question 54 steadily on the manuscript grid
  5. Minutes 48 to 50: Final proofread for missing particles, spelling errors, and plain-style verb endings

Frequently asked questions

What happens if I write fewer than 600 characters?

The official prompt sets the target length at 600 to 700 characters. If your essay stops short of 600 characters, scorers apply tiered deductions. Essays below 500 characters lose substantial points, and writing under 400 characters risks receiving a zero on the task achievement rubric.

Can I use first-person pronouns like 나 or 저?

Avoid 「나」, 「저」, and 「우리」 in formal essays. Instead of writing 「제 생각에는」 (In my opinion), phrase your stance objectively: 「~라고 볼 수 있다」 (It can be viewed that ~) or 「~라는 점에 주목해야 한다」 (We must pay attention to the fact that ~). Refer to society as 「현대 사회의 구성원」 or 「사람들」 rather than our group.

Should I write a separate title on the top line of the grid?

No. Unlike Korean school writing contests, TOPIK Question 54 does not require a title. Begin immediately on the first line with an indented square and your opening introduction sentence. Writing a title wastes valuable manuscript space.

Quick self-check quiz

Check your knowledge of TOPIK Question 54 essay rules:

  1. 1. 원고지에서 문단이 바뀔 때 첫 칸은: (비워 둔다 / 채워 쓴다)
  2. 2. 학술 논술문 종결 어미로 알맞은 것은: (중요합니다 / 중요하다 / 중요해요)
  3. 3. 본론 문단을 구성할 때 가장 좋은 기준은: (문제에 제시된 소주제 질문들 / 떠오르는 생각 순서)
  4. 4. 서론을 작성할 때 피해야 할 것은: (문제지 지문 문장 그대로 베껴 쓰기 / 화제 제시하기)
Quiz answers and explanations1. 비워 둔다 — indent the first square of every new paragraph by one block. 2. 중요하다 — adjectives in plain style take -다 directly without ㄴ/는. 3. 문제에 제시된 소주제 질문들 — each sub-question bullet should form its own body paragraph. 4. 문제지 지문 문장 그대로 베껴 쓰기 — copied sentences are excluded from character count.

item.title: -세요 and its family: requests, prohibitions, and permissions
item.description: Almost every Korean learner memorises -세요 first, but asking, forbidding, permitting, and restricting each use distinct grammar patterns. Here is the whole family laid out side by side.
item.content:encoded:
Virtually every beginner learns 「-세요」 during their first Korean lesson. But in everyday interactions, knowing how to ask politely is only one piece of the puzzle. You also need to know how to decline an action, ask for permission, and warn someone about rules.

Because these patterns share a courteous tone and often occur together in cafes and airports, learners easily confuse their functions. Here is the entire family compared side by side.

1. Polite requests: -(으)세요

Use 「-(으)세요」 to politely ask someone to perform an action or give instructions. Because it incorporates the subject honorific 「-(으)시-」, it is perfectly safe to use with elders, teachers, and store clerks.

여기에 이름을 써 주세요.Please write your name here.

Note the attachment rule: verb stems ending in a vowel take 「-세요」 (가다 → 가세요), while stems ending in a consonant take 「-으세요」 (앉다 → 앉으세요). Verbs with a ㄹ final consonant drop the ㄹ entirely before attaching 세요 (만들다 → 만드세요, 살다 → 사세요).

Demands, Obligations, Permission and ProhibitionV-(으)세요Asks or tells someone to do something, politely. It also raises the listener.Learn how polite imperative endings attach to consonant and vowel stemsWrite your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for

The two faces of -(으)세요: request vs honorific statement

A frequent point of confusion for beginners is that 「-(으)세요」 serves two distinct grammatical roles depending on intonation and context.

First, it acts as a polite imperative or request: 「조용히 하세요」 (Please be quiet). Second, when used with elders or respected subjects, it functions as a regular present-tense honorific statement or question: 「선생님, 지금 어디 가세요?」 means "Teacher, where are you going?", not "Teacher, please go somewhere!".

2. Polite negative requests: -지 마세요

English speakers often try to make negative requests by adding 「안」 in front of -세요 (like 안 가세요, which means "Are you not leaving?"). To tell someone politely not to do something, use 「-지 마세요」.

여기에 주차하지 마세요.Please do not park here.
너무 걱정하지 마세요.Please do not worry too much.
Demands, Obligations, Permission and ProhibitionV-지 마세요A polite way to tell or ask someone not to do something.Notice how negative requests attach uniformly to verb stems without sound changesWrite your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for

3. Granting and asking permission: -아/어도 되다

While -세요 directs an action, 「-아/어도 되다」 removes an obstacle. It tells the listener that doing something is completely fine.

여기 앉으세요. (Request: Please take a seat here.)
여기 앉아도 돼요. (Permission: You may sit here if you like.)
사진을 찍어도 돼요? (Question: May I take photos?)

In public facilities, museums, and cafes, asking 「-아/어도 돼요?」 is the standard way to verify whether an action is permitted before proceeding.

Trying New Things and ExperiencesV-아/어 보다Means trying something out. It is also often used when making suggestions.Examine how permission questions work in restaurants and museumsWrite your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for

4. Stating rules and boundaries: -(으)면 안 되다

When an action violates rules, safety guidelines, or social etiquette, use 「-(으)면 안 되다」. While -지 마세요 is a polite personal plea, -(으)면 안 되다 states that an action is objectively forbidden.

여기서 담배를 피우면 안 돼요.You must not smoke here.
시험 중에 휴대전화를 사용하면 안 됩니다.You must not use mobile phones during the exam.
Trying New Things and ExperiencesV-(으)ㄴ 적이 있다/없다Expresses past experience by stating whether something has happened or not.Study how strict prohibitions and societal rules are expressedWrite your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for

Polite requests for help: -아/어 주세요 vs -(으)세요

Compare 「이 책을 읽으세요」 and 「이 책을 읽어 주세요」. The first is an instruction: "Please read this book (for your own benefit)". The second is a personal favor: "Please read this book (for me / help me out)".

Whenever you ask someone to do something that benefits you personally — such as fetching water, translating a phrase, or opening a door — pair the verb with 「-아/어 주다」 before attaching -세요. In restaurants, say 「물 좀 주세요」 (Please give me water) or 「메뉴판 좀 보여 주세요」 (Please show me the menu).

Formal announcements: -(으)십시오 vs -(으)세요

On public transit announcements, in written safety manuals, and across news broadcasts, you will rarely hear 「-(으)세요」. Instead, official Korean relies on 「-(으)십시오」.

출입문이 닫힙니다. 안전선 밖으로 물러서 주십시오. (Official subway announcement: Doors closing. Please step behind the safety line.)
비상구 위치를 확인하십시오. (Flight safety manual: Please check the emergency exit location.)

Use 「-(으)세요」 in spoken conversations with real human beings in front of you. Reserve 「-(으)십시오」 for public addresses, formal speeches, and printed notices.

Real-world dialogues in cafes and offices

Notice how these four grammar patterns interact dynamically during daily routines:

🧀저기요, 여기 노트북 충전기 꽂아도 돼요?
🥔네, 저쪽 벽에 있는 콘센트 쓰세요.

The customer asks for permission using 「꽂아도 돼요?」, and the barista grants it while offering a polite direction with 「쓰세요」.

🧀회의실 불을 끄고 나갈까요?
🥔아직 다른 팀이 회의 중이니까 불 끄지 마세요.

Colleague B prevents an inconvenient action with the gentle negative request 「불 끄지 마세요」.

Frequently asked questions

Can I use -세요 when asking my boss or professor for a favor?

While -세요 is polite, giving a bare imperative to someone of much higher status can sound slightly direct. When asking a superior or professor for assistance, Korean speakers soften the request by adding conditional or question endings: 「확인해 주실 수 있으세요?」 (Could you possibly check this?) or 「검토해 주시겠어요?」 (Would you mind reviewing this?).

What is the difference between 하지 마세요 and 하면 안 돼요?

「하지 마세요」 is an interpersonal request asking someone to refrain from an action ("Please do not do that"). 「하면 안 돼요」 is an objective rule stating that the action is impermissible under company policy, law, or etiquette ("You cannot do that / it is against regulations").

Why do some verbs change completely with -세요?

Certain common verbs have specialized honorific replacement stems. For example, instead of 먹으세요, native speakers use 「드세요」 (or 「잡수세요」). Instead of 자세요, use 「주무세요」. Instead of 있으세요 when asking someone to stay, use 「계세요」 (as in 안녕히 계세요).

Quick self-check quiz

Select the most appropriate pattern for each real-life scenario:

  1. 1. 도서관에서 친구에게 조용히 하라고 부탁할 때: (조용히 하세요 / 조용히 하면 안 돼요)
  2. 2. 미술관에서 플래시 촬영이 금지되어 있음을 안내할 때: (촬영하지 마세요 / 촬영하면 안 됩니다)
  3. 3. 식당에서 빈자리에 앉아도 되는지 물어볼 때: (앉으세요? / 앉아도 돼요?)
  4. 4. 추운 날씨에 감기 걸리지 말라고 당부할 때: (감기 걸리지 마세요 / 감기 걸리면 안 돼요)
Quiz answers and explanations1. 조용히 하세요 — direct polite request to a peer. 2. 촬영하면 안 됩니다 — official rule/prohibition in a museum. 3. 앉아도 돼요? — checking permission before sitting. 4. 감기 걸리지 마세요 — caring personal wish and request.

Next time you are at a cafe in Seoul: ask for water with 「-아/어 주세요」, check if you can plug in your laptop with 「-아/어도 돼요?」, and look out for 「-지 마세요」 on signs.

item.title: 안 vs 못: two ways to say "not" in Korean
item.description: Translation apps render both as "I do not", but confusing 안 and 못 can make you sound accidentally cold or rude. Here is the distinction between choice and ability.
item.content:encoded:
Compare 「저는 매운 음식을 안 먹어요」 and 「저는 매운 음식을 못 먹어요」. English translation tools often render both sentences as "I do not eat spicy food". Yet to a native Korean speaker, they convey fundamentally different attitudes.

In Korean, negation divides cleanly along one question: is this your deliberate choice, or an external inability?

안: Negation of will and choice

「안」 expresses that you are capable of doing something, but actively choose not to. It indicates intention, decision, or personal preference.

저는 커피를 안 마셔요.I do not drink coffee. (by personal choice)
주말에는 일을 안 해요.I do not work on weekends. (my decision)
Negative Expressions단어 부정 (있다↔없다, 알다↔모르다)Words that have their own distinct antonyms instead of taking the negative prefix 「안」.Examine how short negation and long negation patterns express personal decisionsWrite your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for

못: Negation of ability and circumstance

「못」 indicates that regardless of your desire, external circumstances, physical limitations, or lack of skill prevent you from doing it.

감기에 걸려서 학교에 못 갔어요.I caught a cold, so I could not go to school.
한국어를 아직 잘 못해요.I cannot speak Korean well yet.
Negative Expressions안 A/V-아/어요Expresses simple negative action or your intention not to do something.Learn how inability and situational obstacles differ from voluntary choicesWrite your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for

Why confusing them causes social awkwardness

Suppose a coworker invites you to dinner tonight. If you reply 「오늘 안 가요」, you are saying "I choose not to go" — which sounds blunt, almost dismissive. If you say 「오늘 선약이 있어서 못 가요」 (I have a prior engagement, so I cannot go), you express that you would attend if you were free.

🧀오늘 저녁에 같이 밥 먹을래요?
🥔미안해요, 약속이 있어서 오늘은 못 가요.

Adjectives take 안, not 못

Because adjectives describe states rather than intentional actions, adjectives almost never take 「못」.

날씨가 안 좋아요. (Correct: The weather is not good.)
날씨가 못 좋아요. (Incorrect — weather has no ability or skill.)
방이 안 넓어요. (Correct: The room is not spacious.)

Adjectives describe inherent qualities, measurements, emotions, or environmental conditions. Since a room cannot exert willpower or possess physical capability, saying 「방이 못 넓어요」 makes no sense in Korean. When negating descriptive verbs, always stick to 「안」 or the long form 「-지 않다」.

Word order trap: noun + 하다 compound verbs

A frequent error among beginner learners involves placing the negative adverb before compound verbs that end in 「하다」. Verbs like 「공부하다」 (to study), 「운동하다」 (to exercise), and 「요리하다」 (to cook) consist of an independent Sino-Korean noun combined with the verb 「하다」.

In short negation with 「안」 and 「못」, the adverb must slip inside the compound, directly before 「하다」.

  • 공부 안 해요 (Correct: I do not study) vs 안 공부해요 (Incorrect)
  • 운동 못해요 (Correct: I cannot exercise) vs 못 운동해요 (Incorrect)
  • 요리 안 해요 (Correct: I do not cook) vs 안 요리해요 (Incorrect)
  • 수영 못해요 (Correct: I cannot swim) vs 못 수영해요 (Incorrect)

Pure native verbs ending in 하다, such as 「좋아하다」 (to like) and 「싫어하다」 (to dislike), are single unbreakable words. For those verbs, place the adverb right at the front: 「안 좋아해요」 (I do not like it).

Short negation vs long negation: 안 vs -지 않다 and 못 vs -지 못하다

Korean offers two structural styles of negation: short negation placed directly in front of the verb, and long negation attached as an ending to the verb stem.

Short negation with 「안」 and 「못」 belongs primarily to spontaneous spoken conversation, text messages, and casual daily chats. Long negation with 「-지 않다」 and 「-지 못하다」 sounds more deliberate, formal, and objective.

회의에 참석하지 못했습니다.I was unable to attend the meeting. (formal written register)
비가 오지 않습니다.It is not raining. (official announcement or formal statement)

In formal presentations, business reports, news broadcasts, and TOPIK essays, long negation is strongly preferred. In everyday exchanges with friends, shopkeepers, and coworkers, short negation is the natural default.

The tricky spelling: 못하다 vs 못 하다

Korean orthography distinguishes between the single compound verb 「못하다」 (written without a space) and the adverb phrase 「못 하다」 (written with a space).

When you write 「못하다」 as one word, it means to perform poorly or lack proficiency: 「노래를 못해요」 means "I am bad at singing", and 「수학을 못해요」 means "I am poor at maths". When you write 「못 하다」 with a space, it indicates that a circumstance physically prevents you from performing the act: 「시간이 없어서 숙제를 못 했어요」 means "Because I had no time, I could not do the homework".

Real-life dialogues: dietary choices and polite refusals

Notice how native speakers shift between 「안」 and 「못」 depending on whether they are expressing an ethical preference, a biological limitation, or a polite scheduling conflict.

🧀돼지고기 드실 수 있어요?
🥔종교적인 이유로 돼지고기는 안 먹어요.

In the exchange above, Person B chooses 「안 먹어요」 because following a religious dietary rule represents a conscious commitment rather than a physical inability. Compare that with an allergy scenario below:

🧀땅콩 아이스크림 주문할까요?
🥔제가 견과류 알레르기가 있어서 못 먹어요.

Because food allergies cause severe medical reactions, Person B uses 「못 먹어요」. Saying 「안 먹어요」 in an allergy context would fail to communicate the biological danger.

Frequently asked questions

Is 못 more polite than 안 when turning down an invitation?

Yes, in social contexts turning down an invitation with 「못 가요」 sounds significantly softer than 「안 가요」. Using 「안 가요」 implies that you simply do not want to see the person or attend the event. Using 「못 가요」 signals that you would love to join if circumstances permitted.

Can I use 못 with verbs of knowing like 알다?

No. The verb 「알다」 (to know) does not take 「못」 or 「안」 in modern standard Korean. Instead, Korean uses the dedicated antonym verb 「모르다」 (to not know). You never say 「못 알아요」 or 「안 알아요」; you simply say 「몰라요」.

What about 있다 and 없다?

Similarly, 「있다」 (to exist, to have) has its own lexical opposite 「없다」 (to not exist, to lack). Native speakers never say 「안 있어요」 or 「못 있어요」 to indicate absence; they say 「없어요」.

Quick self-check quiz

Test your understanding by choosing between 안 and 못 for each sentence below:

  1. 1. 다리를 다쳐서 축구를 (안 / 못) 해요.
  2. 2. 저는 건강을 위해서 탄산음료를 (안 / 못) 마셔요.
  3. 3. 이 치마는 허리가 너무 좁아서 (안 / 못) 맞아요.
  4. 4. 오늘 너무 바빠서 점심을 (안 / 못) 먹었어요.
Quiz answers and explanations1. 못 — an injured leg is a physical obstacle. 2. 안 — giving up soda for health is a conscious personal lifestyle choice. 3. 안 — 맞다 in the sense of fitting is descriptive, so it takes 안. 4. 못 — severe busyness prevented eating lunch despite hunger.

Remember: use 「안」 for deliberate decisions and descriptive adjectives. Reserve 「못」 when physical limits, skill, or busy schedules hold you back.

item.title: Saying "because" in Korean: -아서 vs -니까
item.description: Both translate as "because" in English, yet swapping them creates awkward sentences. Here are three practical tests to choose the right cause connector every time.
item.content:encoded:
Compare two common phrases: 「늦어서 죄송합니다」 and 「늦었으니까 죄송합니다」. The first is textbook natural Korean. The second sounds defensive, almost like arguing. Yet English dictionaries translate both endings simply as "because".

Learners struggle with Korean reason connectors not because the concepts differ, but because each grammar pattern imposes strict constraints on what type of clause can follow.

Rule 1: Use -(으)니까 with commands and suggestions

This single boundary resolves 80 percent of learner mistakes. Whenever the second half of your sentence is an imperative, suggestion, or request ending in 「-세요」, 「-(으)ㅂ시다」, or 「-(으)ㄹ까요?」, you cannot use 「-아/어서」.

비가 오니까 우산을 가져가세요. (Correct: It is raining, so take an umbrella.)
비가 와서 우산을 가져가세요. (Incorrect — native speakers never say this.)

Notice this on subway announcements and road signs: 「위험하니까 조심하세요」 (It is dangerous, so please be careful). In customer service and safety instructions, 「-(으)니까」 is standard.

Reasons and CausesA/V-(으)니까 ①Gives a reason. Unlike 「-아/어서」, a request or a suggestion can follow.Notice how commands and proposals naturally pair with this endingWrite your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for

Rule 2: Use -아/어서 for greetings, apologies, and thanks

Social formulas require 「-아/어서」. Using 「-(으)니까」 when apologising or thanking someone makes it sound as though you are presenting an intellectual argument rather than expressing sincere emotion.

늦어서 죄송합니다.Sorry for being late.
도와주셔서 감사합니다.Thank you for helping me.
만나서 반갑습니다.Nice to meet you.

Saying 「도와줬으니까 감사합니다」 sounds bizarrely transactional. Memorise these everyday courtesy phrases as single chunks.

Reasons and CausesA/V-아/어서 (이유)States that something happened because of this reason. It is the most basic way to express cause.Review standard cause-and-effect clauses used in daily conversationWrite your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for

Rule 3: Past tense marking differs

Never attach past tense markers 「-았/었-」 directly inside 「-아/어서」. The tense is marked only on the final verb at the end of the sentence.

바빠서 못 갔어요. (Correct: I was busy, so I could not go.)
바빴어서 못 갔어요. (Incorrect — double past tense is redundant.)
어제 바빴으니까 오늘은 쉴게요. (Correct — -(으)니까 accepts past tense freely.)

Because 「-아/어서」 establishes a continuous sequential relationship where the first event naturally flows into the second, Korean grammar requires the entire sentence to share the tense of the concluding verb. Marking the past inside 「-아/어서」 is grammatically invalid on formal proficiency tests like TOPIK.

Objective cause vs subjective reasoning

Beyond grammar rules, a subtle difference in attitude separates these two endings. 「-아/어서」 presents an objective, widely accepted natural consequence. Anyone looking at the situation would agree with the link.

배가 너무 아파서 병원에 다녀왔어요.My stomach hurt so much that I went to the hospital.

By contrast, 「-(으)니까」 highlights the speaker's personal judgment, observation, or deduction. The reason serves as justification for what the speaker believes or proposes.

제가 직접 먹어 보니까 아주 맛있더라고요.I tasted it myself, and found it delicious.

What about 때문에 and -기 때문에?

「때문에」 connects directly to nouns (비 때문에), or to verbs using 「-기 때문에」 (춥기 때문에). It provides a neutral, objective explanation and is especially common in formal writing and news broadcasts.

폭설 때문에 비행기가 결항되었습니다.Due to heavy snowfall, flights were cancelled.
물가가 올랐기 때문에 소비가 줄어들었습니다.Because prices rose, consumer spending declined.
Reasons and CausesN 때문에, A/V-기 때문에Names the cause plainly. Common in writing.Learn formal noun and verb combinations used in essays and newsWrite your own sentence with this →Form, examples and what to watch out for

The busy excuse trap: -느라고 vs -아/어서

Intermediate learners often encounter another reason connector: 「-느라고」. While 「-아/어서」 simply links a cause to an effect, 「-느라고」 specifies that focusing your energy on one active task directly caused a negative outcome or prevented you from doing something else.

시험공부를 하느라고 어젯밤에 잠을 못 잤어요.Because I was studying for the exam, I could not sleep last night.

Notice two strict restrictions: the subject of both clauses must be the identical person, and the second clause must describe an undesirable consequence or sacrifice. You cannot use 「-느라고」 with adjectives or positive results. For simple neutral facts, stick with 「-아/어서」.

Side-by-side comparison summary

  • -아/어서: Objective cause, apologies and thanks, strictly NO past tense in clause 1, NO imperatives or suggestions in clause 2
  • -(으)니까: Subjective reasoning and discovery, allows past tense (-았/었으니까), MANDATORY for imperatives (-세요) and suggestions (-ㅂ시다)
  • -기 때문에: Formal and written cause, objective facts, pairs with nouns directly (N 때문에), common in reports and essays

Real-world dialogues: choosing the right connector

Listen to how native speakers switch between connectors in common daily interactions:

🧀이번 주말에 등산하러 갈까요?
🥔날씨가 추우니까 따뜻하게 입고 오세요.

Because Person B provides a piece of advice ending in the imperative 「입고 오세요」, only 「추우니까」 fits. Using 「추워서」 here would sound unnatural.

🧀민수 씨, 어제 동창 모임에 왜 안 왔어요?
🥔갑자기 회사에 급한 일이 생겨서 못 갔어요.

In reporting an objective sequence of events explaining why one missed a gathering, 「일이 생겨서」 provides the courteous, natural answer.

Frequently asked questions

Can I use -아/어서 when asking someone out for lunch?

No. If you want to invite someone by saying "I am hungry, so shall we eat?", you must use 「-(으)니까」: 「배고프니까 같이 밥 먹을까요?」. Because the sentence ends with a suggestion 「-(으)ㄹ까요?」, 「배고파서 같이 밥 먹을까요?」 is ungrammatical.

Why do I hear Koreans say 바빴어서 on TV dramas?

In colloquial casual speech, some native speakers slip into double past tense marking like 「피곤했어서」 or 「바빴어서」 to emphasize that the state occurred in the remote past. However, Korean language institutes and TOPIK examiners strictly classify this as colloquial error. In formal writing, interviews, and language exams, stick firmly to 「피곤해서」.

How do I choose between (이)라서 and (이)기 때문에 for nouns?

With nouns, 「(이)라서」 represents the spoken colloquial form of -아/어서: 「주말이라서 길이 막혀요」 (It is the weekend, so roads are congested). By contrast, 「명사 + 때문에」 or 「명사 + (이)기 때문에」 represents formal and written style: 「주말 때문에」 or 「주말이기 때문에」. Use 「(이)라서」 in daily chat and 「때문에」 in formal reports.

Quick self-check quiz

Choose the correct ending for each sentence below:

  1. 1. 길이 많이 (막혀서 / 막히니까) 지하철을 탑시다.
  2. 2. 초대해 주 (셔서 / 시니까) 진심으로 감사드립니다.
  3. 3. 어제 비가 많이 (와서 / 왔어서) 야구 경기가 취소되었어요.
  4. 4. 창밖을 (보니까 / 봐서) 눈이 하얗게 쌓여 있었어요.
Quiz answers and explanations1. 막히니까 — ending in proposal 탑시다 requires -(으)니까. 2. 셔서 — expressions of gratitude require -아/어서. 3. 와서 — standard past causal clause without double past marking. 4. 보니까 — discovering a situation upon looking calls for -(으)니까.
